subject: anaesthesia
title: Adrenal Suppression, Alpha-2 Agonist Dexmedetomidine, and Midazolam

steps.title: Etomidate Adrenal Enzyme Blockade
steps.tx: **Adrenal suppression by etomidate** results from potent, dose-dependent, reversible inhibition of 11-beta-hydroxylase (CYP11B1), the mitochondrial cytochrome P450 enzyme converting 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol and 11-deoxycorticosterone to corticosterone in the adrenal cortex. A single induction bolus of 0.3 mg/kg suppresses cortisol and aldosterone synthesis for 24 to 48 hours, rendering patients unresponsive to adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulation.

A single induction bolus of 0.3 mg/kg suppresses cortisol and aldosterone synthesis for 24 to 48 hours, rendering patients unresponsive to adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH) stimulation.

rows: Severe blunting of physiological stress cortisol surge
Transient impairment of renal sodium conservation
Sharp doubling of serum cortisol levels
Flat refractory response across 24 to 48 hours

steps.title: ICU Septic Shock Controversy
steps.tx: **Etomidate mortality hazard in septic shock** was first uncovered when continuous ICU etomidate infusions quadrupled mortality in trauma and intensive care patients due to total adrenocortical exhaustion. Even a single induction bolus for emergency intubation in septic shock significantly increases vasopressor dependency and 28-day mortality, leading international sepsis guidelines to strongly recommend ketamine over etomidate.

left.title: Etomidate in Septic Shock
points: Abolishes essential physiological stress cortisol secretion
Blunts vascular responsiveness to endogenous catecholamines
Prolongs required duration of high-dose noradrenaline infusions

right.title: Ketamine Alternative in Sepsis
points: Zero adrenal enzyme inhibition; preserves endogenous cortisol
Maintains systemic hemodynamics through sympathetic tone
Favoured induction agent in emergency septic intubation

steps.title: Dexmedetomidine Receptor Selectivity
steps.tx: **Dexmedetomidine alpha-2 receptor selectivity** exhibits an extraordinary 1,600:1 selectivity ratio for alpha-2 over alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, making it eight times more selective than clonidine (220:1 ratio). Dexmedetomidine acts predominantly on presynaptic alpha-2A receptors in the locus coeruleus of the brainstem, inhibiting adenylate cyclase and terminating neuronal noradrenaline release, generating biomimetic non-rapid eye movement (NREM stage 2) sleep.

steps.title: Cooperative Sedation Mechanics
steps.tx: **Cooperative sedation with dexmedetomidine** provides a calm, tranquil state from which patients can be immediately awakened by verbal commands, perform complex cognitive tasks or neurological examinations, and smoothly transition back into sleep once stimulation ceases. Because ventilation is spared, it serves as the premier sedative for awake fiberoptic intubation, awake craniotomy brain mapping, and non-invasive ventilation weaning.

nodes.label: Infuse dexmedetomidine 0.5 to 1 mcg/kg over 10 minutes
Presynaptic alpha-2 activation in locus coeruleus
Induce physiological NREM sleep without respiratory depression
Patient awakens instantly upon gentle verbal command

steps.title: Biphasic Hemodynamic Response
steps.tx: **Biphasic blood pressure response of dexmedetomidine** occurs during rapid intravenous loading boluses: initial stimulation of peripheral vascular smooth muscle alpha-2B receptors produces transient vasoconstriction and hypertension, triggering reflex baroreceptor bradycardia. Subsequently, as central presynaptic alpha-2A sympatholysis dominates in the locus coeruleus, sustained moderate hypotension and bradycardia ensue, mandating slow loading infusions over 10 to 15 minutes.

left.title: Initial Peripheral Phase (Minutes 1 to 3)
points: Direct activation of vascular alpha-2B receptors
Reflex vagal bradycardia mediated by aortic baroreceptors

right.title: Subsequent Central Phase (Minutes 5 to 60)
points: Central sympatholysis via locus coeruleus alpha-2A agonism
Sustained moderate drop in systemic vascular resistance
Mild sinus bradycardia responding to glycopyrrolate if severe

steps.title: Opioid and Anaesthetic Sparing
steps.tx: **Opioid-sparing analgesia of dexmedetomidine** stems from stimulation of alpha-2 receptors located in the substantia gelatinosa of the spinal cord dorsal horn, blunting primary afferent nociceptive neurotransmitter release. Co-administration slashes intraoperative volatile anaesthetic MAC requirements by up to 50 percent and reduces postoperative opioid consumption, diminishing opioid-induced respiratory depression and bowel ileus.

rows: Reduces requirement down to 0.5 to 0.6 MAC
Slashes opioid demands by 30 to 50 percent
Zero respiratory depression during skull opening
Halves the incidence of ICU delirium

steps.title: Midazolam Water Solubility Transition
steps.tx: **Midazolam pH-dependent ring opening** gives it unique physical properties: at an acidic ampoule pH under 4.0, its imidazole ring remains open, rendering midazolam completely water-soluble and eliminating the need for organic solvent vehicles like propylene glycol, preventing venous thrombophlebitis. Upon injection into physiological blood at pH 7.4, the imidazole ring spontaneously snaps closed, converting midazolam into a highly lipophilic molecule that crosses the blood-brain barrier rapidly.

nodes.label: Midazolam in acidic vial (pH <4.0) has open imidazole ring

Ring closes spontaneously; lipophilic molecule enters brain in 60s

steps.title: Flumazenil Specific Antidote
steps.tx: **Flumazenil competitive benzodiazepine antagonism** selectively binds the benzodiazepine recognition site on the GABA-A receptor, competitively displacing midazolam, diazepam, and lorazepam without intrinsic agonist efficacy. Administered intravenously in titrated increments of 0.1 to 0.2 mg every minute (up to 1 mg), flumazenil reverses sedation within two minutes, but its short elimination half-life (under one hour) means resedation can recur after longer-acting benzodiazepines wear off.

left.title: Flumazenil Pharmacokinetics
points: Rapid competitive displacement at GABA-A receptor site
Elimination half-life of only 50 to 60 minutes
Risk of recurrence of sedation as long-acting sedatives persist

right.title: Precaution in Chronic Dependence
points: Strictly contraindicated in chronic benzodiazepine users
Precipitates acute withdrawal seizures and autonomic crisis
Contraindicated in concurrent tricyclic antidepressant overdose
